observed.facings.png: Three facings at one shared scale on a checkerboard. South: a squat green-scaled dragon seen from the front, face to the camera. East: a long, low side profile with the head to the right. North: the rump and back seen from behind. Every facing has the same pale yellow-orange bubbly belly, small bat-like wings, a spiked dorsal ridge, and three small bubbly yellow mash heaps at the feet. Pale yellow-green smoke wisps rise from the head in each view.
observed.south.png: Front view. A broad, horned dragon head with amber eyes faces the camera, with two pale green smoke plumes curling up from the nostrils. Thick yellow foamy slime drips from the jaws. A huge round belly hangs low, covered in translucent golden bubbles and dripping. The legs are thick and splayed with dark claws. Small wings sit at the shoulders, with the membranes partly visible to the sides. Three bubbly mash mounds are on the ground: one under each front foot and one between them. Painterly and detailed, with a slightly grumpy look and no cuteness.
observed.east.png: Side profile. The body is long, low and barrel-bellied, with a heavy dragon head on the right with horns, an amber eye and a slime-drooling muzzle. A smoke wisp rises from the nostril. A small wing is folded flat along the back, too small for flight, and there are dorsal spikes. A short, thick tail stub is on the left. The belly is distended and glistening with golden bubbles and drips. Four thick legs have dark claws. Three mash heaps sit at the feet. Realistic and painterly.
observed.north.png: Rear view. A broad rump with a spiked dorsal ridge running down to a rounded tail base, the two folded wings at the shoulders, and the swollen bubbly belly visible beneath and to the sides. No face and no eyes. A smoke wisp drifts up from the hidden head at top right. Three mash heaps are at the feet.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the drake is about 2.5 cells long, well over twice the length of the vanilla human, and reads as a heavy beast. At 32 px/cell it reads as a green body with an orange-yellow belly and yellow blobs at the feet. The silhouette is clear and stands apart from the ground.

observed.facings.png: Three facings on one shared scale. All three show the same heavy, four-legged creature. Its whole body is covered in rust-brown, cracked, rocky plates, and clusters of pale translucent crystal blades stand along its back. South looks at the blunt wedge-shaped head plate head-on. East is a side profile with the head to the right, the back rising into a hump and crystal fans that grow larger toward the shoulders. North shows the rump and hind legs, with the crystal fans running down the spine's centre line. North looks slightly taller than the others because its crystal stack rises higher.
observed.south.png: A front view. A blunt, eyeless wedge of plates sits low and centred, with no eyes, mouth or nostrils. Thick pillar-like front legs splay out, and the stubby toes are made of rounded stone lumps. Behind the head the largest crystal fan rises in the middle, with smaller fans stepping down on each side. Those side fans are the row of fans down the spine, seen receding from the front. The plates are rust-orange and dark brown with a pitted, scabby texture. The background is transparent, but a faint yellow fringe edges the crystals.
observed.east.png: A side profile facing right. The body is long and low-slung with a sloping rump and a hump over the shoulders. The head is a single blunt plate wedge with no eye. Six crystal fans stand upright along the spine, growing from small at the rear to large over the shoulders. The four columnar legs are plated and end in rounded toe lumps. The plates are irregular slabs of different sizes, with rusty and dark bark-like surfaces. There is no ground or shadow beneath it.
observed.north.png: A rear view. Wide haunches and the hind legs face the camera. A rounded plated rump has a pointed plate where a tail would be, and there is no face. The crystal fans run vertically up the spine's centre line, small at the rump and larger toward the shoulders, and the tallest cluster rises above the back. The plates and colours match the other views. The background is transparent, with a slight yellow fringe on the crystal edges.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the creature fills many cells beside a tiny vanilla human, and the plate texture holds up crisply. At normal play (32 px per cell) it is a huge rust-brown plated beast with a pale crystal ridge, many times the human's size, and it reads clearly against the sand ground.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the blunt head wedge pointing straight at the camera, with the front legs splayed on either side.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the rump, haunches, hind legs and the pointed rear plate. There is no face and no eyes.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three are angled ground-level views of the body, legs and underside. None is a plan view.

SAME_SIZE.seen: The 17% spread comes mostly from north's taller crystal stack and east's lower profile. Body widths and leg heights match closely in the shared-scale panel, so the spread is pose and structure, not a size jump. North reads slightly larger, which is a minor point.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: The same plates, palette, columnar legs and crystal fans appear on every facing. The fan row turns with the body: it recedes behind the head on south, runs lengthwise on east, and runs down the centre line on north.

SIGNATURE.seen: The defining features are clear on every facing: a slag-plate hide, upright crystal fans down the spine and no eyes.

ALIEN.seen: The armoured quadruped body suggests an ankylosaur. But the eyeless rock-slab head, the crystal vent fans and the slag-plate hide make it read as an alien rock beast, not an Earth species.

DEPARTURES.seen: 1) No eyes anywhere: present (the head is a bare plate wedge). 2) Hide of grown-together slag and bark plates: present (irregular cracked rust-and-dark slabs, more slag than bark, but not a shell or scales). 3) A row of crystal fans down the spine: present (six fans on east). 4) A lumpy hill-of-slag silhouette: mostly present (the plated outline is lumpy, though the east back curve is fairly smooth).

STYLE.seen: Painterly and realistic, with a textured stone surface. It is not cute and not cel-shaded. The rendering leans slightly towards a 3D-render look but stays acceptable.

OURS.seen: A unique invented design that matches the description. It is not vanilla or donor art.

ALPHA.seen: The cut-out is transparent with no ground or shadow. There is only a faint yellow edge fringe on the crystal blades.

SCALE.seen: At drawSize 7 it dwarfs the human, which fits 'a hill of slag that moves' and crews climbing it to shear plates.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px per cell it reads as a dark plated mass with a bright crystal ridge, well apart from the ground.
